Patrick Doyle is a Senior Backend Engineer at NexaCorp, leveraging seven years of experience to design scalable, secure, and efficient enterprise systems. His work focuses on optimizing cloud infrastructure, where he reduced AWS costs by 22% through strategic resource allocation and automation. A strong advocate for modular architecture, he led the migration of monolithic services to microservices, improving deployment velocity by 40% and enhancing system resilience.  

Adept at building high-performance APIs, Patrick’s RESTful designs underpin critical integrations across NexaCorp’s platforms, balancing complexity with maintainability. His expertise in Go and Java has driven the development of core services, with Go’s concurrency model cutting processing times by 35% in real-time data pipelines.  

He champions automation, owning CI/CD pipelines that slashed deployment cycles from hours to minutes, while Docker and Kubernetes implementations streamlined container orchestration, reducing environment drift and improving team collaboration.  

Patrick’s proficiency in PostgreSQL ensures robust data management, and his Python scripts automate routine tasks, freeing engineers for higher-impact work. He also oversees monitoring systems, minimizing downtime through proactive alerting and root-cause analysis.  

Driven by pragmatic solutions, he balances technical depth with business outcomes, ensuring systems are both innovative and operationally sound. His approach to infrastructure as code, using Terraform, has standardized environments and cut provisioning time by 50%, aligning engineering efforts with organizational goals.
